blocks.content: No person shall be eligible for election as President unless he is a citizen of India, has completed the age of thirty-five years and is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 58 prescribes the constitutional qualifications required for election as the President of India.
The candidate must be a citizen of India and have completed at least 35 years of age.
The candidate must be qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha (House of the People).
The candidate should not hold any office of profit under the Union government, any state government, or any local or public authority.
A sitting President, Vice-President, Governor of a state, or Minister for the Union or any state is not deemed to hold an office of profit and is eligible for election.

items: Frequent Trap: A presidential candidate must be qualified for membership of the Lok Sabha, whereas a Vice-Presidential candidate must be qualified for the Rajya Sabha.
Minimum Age Distinction: The age requirement is 35 years for the President, compared to 25 years for the Lok Sabha and 30 years for the Rajya Sabha.

Office of Profit Exception: Sitting Ministers, Governors, the President, and the Vice-President can directly contest elections without resigning first, as their posts are not considered offices of profit.
